new_findings.summary: entityVisible3D hides surface enemies standing on ground above h=1.6. This is separate from D7's L511 rule: surface enemies spawn with z:0 (L5893), only underground enemies track floor height (L11458-11460), and drawEnemies3D passes e.z||0 (L14006). The below-floor cull at L508 (wz < floorZ-40) then fires for every enemy on ground where floorZ = 25*h > 40.
new_findings.evidence: Default run: 5 of 23 high-ground surface enemies hidden on Endless seed 424242, e.g. world (-138,-1038) at h=1.79 with e.z=0, and 2 of 28 on 777000. With --seeds 1,777,12345,424242: 9/28, 9/30, 29/50 and 5/23. FIX probe 06 (L508 treats wz 0 as unknown) flips the check to PASS and nothing else.

new_findings.summary: The 3 to 8 cave-floor quads the audit counted from the ramp and the arch (D4) all belong to the arch's open pit (cells with a ceiling but no cap). Zero buried tunnel quads are drawn from the ramp or from inside the arch.
new_findings.evidence: With open-pit cells hidden during the recorded floor pass, the buried count is 0 on all 5 entrances in the sweep (seeds 1, 777 e0 and e1, 12345, 424242). Examples: 12345 ramp 0 (3 counting the pit); 424242 arch 0 (2 counting the pit).

new_findings.summary: Capped cave walls show through from the cap on Cave Test seed 1. This seed is not in the defaults. drawWalls3D's cull at L12052 compares the physics camera height cam.z (60+40h) with the render-unit value wcap*25-2, and these wall cells sit in re-sorted stacks where l0 is the ceiling below a raised floor.
new_findings.evidence: --seeds 1: the camera stands on the cap at world (1074,438), h=1.08. 8 capped-wall fills are drawn from 4 cells at world (810..846,114), wallCapZ 4.30-4.66, stacks like [2@-0.98 1@3.35 4@4.75]. cam.z=103.4 while wcap*25-2 = 105.5..114.5, so the cull never fires. Checked by isolating single wall cells in a scratch script.

concerns: Two checks change game data in memory for the length of one recorded pass, then restore it. (1) The buried-walls check zeroes every uncapped wall cell in grid. (2) The ramp, arch and bleed-through views set layerCount to 0 on open-pit cells (a ceiling with no cap). Hiding pit cells also stops adjacent capped ceiling cells from stitching (findCeilMatchZ returns NaN), which slightly weakens the ceiling half of the bleed-through check at pit edges. The floor half is unaffected, as BREAK probe 02 shows.

The ramp check (D4) is partly about geometry, not only the renderer. On 12345 the tunnel ceiling at the roof start (-1.86) is below the ramp floor you stand on (-0.80). The only one-line change that makes it pass (probe 02) does so by drawing the tunnel through the hill, which breaks the bleed-through guard. A real fix probably needs the mouth geometry fixed as well.

The ramp view stands 24 u outside the first roof cell, not at the audit's fixed +260. On 424242, +260 is already under the roof (roof starts at +384), where the player counts as underground and the check would pass trivially.

The two 'no bleed-through' guards pass on the default seeds, but not every seed. The buried-walls check fails with --seeds 1 (see new_findings), and 777 needed the open-pit exclusion. On seed 777 the ceiling check shows 20 and 12 ceiling quads drawn, so D5 is not universal; the aggregate still fails.

checks.id: loot: cave chest gold rises with chest tier
checks.audit_ref: D22 (L5971 gold = floor(10 + rng*30*difficulty), no goldMult)
checks.measures: Over all cross-tier pairs of gold-paying cave chests whose chunks have getDifficultyAt within 0.1: total gold of the higher-tier chests divided by total gold of the lower-tier chests. Gold comes from collectChest.
checks.measured_detail: 0.92x over 1005 pairs of 190 gold-paying cave chests. Mean gold: common 75.9, uncommon 72.2, rare 57.7, epic 64.0. The same statistic on surface chests is 1.40x. Other seed sets: 1.03x (seeds 1,777) and 0.95x (4 seeds).

Any per-tier multiplier of at least 1.33x per step (goldMult 1/1.5/2/3 is at least 1.33 for every pair) gives 1.33x or more; tier-blind gold gives about 1.0x. Pairs are difficulty-matched because gold also scales with difficulty. Pairwise concordance is kept only as a METRIC: a 1.33-1.5x multiplier on a uniform roll caps it near 0.63-0.67, too close to 0.5 to gate on (surface measured 0.71).

concerns: Overlap: tools/webui/harness/game_persistence_harness.js (another suite) has checks at its lines 505/592/594 for collected-chest and swapped-item persistence. My four persistence checks independently confirm the same two swap defects. The orchestrator may want to keep them in only one suite, so a fix does not have to clear two KNOWN_BUGS lists.

The keyboard E path (anonymous keydown listener, L22309-22337) cannot be reached: _game_env's document.addEventListener is a no-op stub, and the required 3-line file header runs LAB.load before a harness could capture listeners. Looting uses the device's gamepad-A path in handleInput (L19098-19099), which runs the same `collectChest(nearestOpenChest)` branch.

The gpLast default {buttons:0} is active-low, so it reads as every button held. Harness-side, START (bit 16) toggles menuOpen as soon as a pad reports valid, and SELECT toggles CONTROL_MODE on the first handleInput (logged '[CTRL] toggled CONTROL_MODE= 1'). I worked around it locally with releasePad(). The same SELECT edge fires in the live page at game start when no pad has been polled (L998, L19000-19010, lastSelectDown reset at L22001/22031); I did not measure any gameplay impact, so it is not reported as a finding.

Cave chests are identified as chunk chests within 12 u of a terminal-chamber centre (today they sit exactly on it, L5970). If a fix moves them further off-centre, the samples shrink and the checks fail loudly with PRECONDITION text rather than passing silently.

The terminal-chamber check is judged on the Cave Test worlds only, where surfaceChests is off so every chest is a cave chest. For Endless it is METRIC-only (16/187 without a chest), because a surface chest lying over a chamber would be indistinguishable there. The reserve-filter cause of that check appears only with --seeds 777; the default seeds exercise only the edge-ring cause.

The gold-by-tier verdict uses a difficulty-matched pair ratio with a 1.2x bar. Tier-blind cave gold measured 0.92-1.03x across seed sets, and the surface reference 1.40-1.62x. An implementation using less than about 1.2x per tier step would fail by design.
The epic-cave check requires EVERY epic cave chest to give a relic or equipment, mirroring the surface rule (every surface epic gets a relic). It is stricter than 'at least one'.

The Z-gate FIX probe gates on getFloorHeightAt (l0TopZ), which the audit calls blind (l0 can be a ceiling). It works here because l0 is the cave floor at every tested chest cell. It only shows the check flips under a Z gate and is not a recommended fix.

The reserve regression guard injects two synthetic chests into chunk data. No naturally generated chest falls in a reserve in the default worlds (metric = 0), so without injection the check would be vacuous.

The floor and cap passes reset equipment to empty slots before each A press (a fresh character), so relic and equipment chests are takes, not swaps. Chests with another chest within 120 u are excluded from the offer tests (10 in Endless 424242), because nearestOpenChest legitimately targets the closer one.

D22's 'all tiers mean 24.4 gold' is not reproduced exactly: Cave Test cave-chest means by tier are 41/27.2/27.8/16 (n=19), and the Endless means are much higher because difficulty reaches about 5 at 20 km. This is consistent with tier-blind gold, so it is not listed as a contradiction.
env_requests: _commonAfterStart should park the gamepad at all-released, gpLast = {x:0,y:0,buttons:-1,valid:false}. The default buttons:0 reads as every button held (active-low): SELECT toggles CONTROL_MODE on the first tick, and START toggles menuOpen as soon as valid is true.
A LAB.pressPad(BTN_*) helper that drives one press and release through handleInput with USE_GAMEPAD=true and USE_MOUSE=false, restoring state afterwards (the local pressA() in game_loot_harness.js).

Capture document/window addEventListener registrations in _game_env before LAB.load (e.g. LAB.listeners.keydown), so harnesses can dispatch real keydown events such as E-to-loot through the page's own handler.

A LAB.windowEntityAt(array, wx, wy) lookup by WORLD coords, plus a return flag from placeWorld saying whether the window re-centred. Window entity arrays are rebuilt on every re-centre, so held object references silently go stale; this caused my first persistence probe to measure the wrong object.

new_findings.summary: An airborne player snaps UP onto a floor above in a single tick. The landing branch of step() calls getWalkableLayerTopAt at the player's height, which accepts a floor up to STEP_UP 1.0 above, then sets pos.floorZ = groundZ with no easing (L10146-10159). This is a second cause of per-tick height jolts, separate from D1's {topH:0} fallback.

The next tick h is -3.549 (dh +0.537) with airborne=false. The picker result for that tick, called with the pre-tick h, is walk idx 0. The harness tags this tick as 'airborne landing snaps UP' in the dh check detail.

checks.id: physics: walking up a rise steeper than STEP_UP never sinks the feet below the ground or the eye into the terrain

Each rise is walked with LAB.walkTo from the neighbour's centre to 3 cells beyond, then the player stands 0.5 s. The chasing enemy just shoves the player along at about 20-30 u/s, and hits only land once the player is pinned against a wall.

All 4 types landed 0 hits: Scout closest 16.33 u (reach 12.4), Soldier 18.71 u (14), Brute 22.40 u (17.2), Wolf 16.62 u (13.2), after 1.6-5.6 s within 30 u. The same pattern holds on --seeds 12345. audit_contradictions: D15 says 'stale reads after assembleWindow'. Measured: 0 stale getFloorHeightAt reads after assembleWindow returns in all 3 real-frame crossings (0/640k, 0/840k, 0/618k reads over 30 frames, including a sweep of all 78,400 cells right after it returned, the player's cell included). The stale reads happen only INSIDE assembleWindow's wallFaceBase precompute (67/45/23 reads, L6844-6861). Its ~70-90k reads evict all 1024 cache slots before it returns. So the lasting damage is wallFaceBase (22/16/16 faces), not later physics reads. A tick-less cache mutation also left 0 stale cells after return.

D12 says 'micro-falls on every downhill cell edge'. On the 4 walked lines: 45 airborne episodes across 238 downhill cell edges, of which 121 drop more than the 0.075 h threshold. Many edges are crossed while already airborne. Every episode is a micro-fall (drop <= 1.0 h), so the bug is real, but it does not fire on every edge.
concerns: step() skips grid-wall collision whenever pos.floorZ > 80, i.e. terrain h > 0.5 (L10206 'aboveWalls'). That covers most raised Endless terrain. In scratch runs with floorZ > 80 on every tick, walls still stayed solid only because the rect-based walls[] pass (L10310-10327) and repelFromWalls catch the player. The PASSing wall check guards the outcome, not which mechanism produces it.

The death check's Scout variant (b) holds health at 5 each tick until the Scout connects, because regen would otherwise make the hit non-lethal. Given the enemy-reach finding, that lethal hit lands only after the Scout pins the player against a wall. That is fine for testing death, but it is not an open-ground hit.
Movement scenarios remove all enemies (enemies = []) each tick, so walks measure terrain physics, not shoves. The combat scenarios add back exactly one enemy.

With --seeds, the same list replaces both the Cave Test and the Endless seeds, and scenarios E/F/G use the first seed. A world with no steep rise, crossing line or descending line reports a PRECONDITION FAILED detail rather than passing vacuously. A sweep with --seeds 12345,1,777,424242 ran every scenario to completion, and F1 kept its verdict.

Sibling suites exist (game_enemies_harness.js, game_caves_*). The enemy-reach check may overlap the enemies suite's scope. It is kept here because it is a player/enemy collision radius issue and explains why death needs a pinned player.

new_findings.summary: Two entrance trees of one network get independent depths, so the cave floor has flat-to-flat cliffs where they meet
new_findings.evidence: Each stack item draws depth 6.0 + rng()*2.5 (L4496) and branches inherit it (L4555). queryCaveGeometry takes the depth of the single max-fade feature (L4693-4694 / L4711-4712), not a blend. Cave Test 777 is one network with two entrances whose cave floors are -7.19 and -8.14; it has a 0.95 h cliff at (378,474)->(378,486) (-7.16 | -8.14). Normal 999983 r3,-4: 1.56 h at (4782,-5286)->(4782,-5274) (-6.28 | -7.86). Normal 424242 r0,-11 (sweep): 1.48 h at x=954->966, y=-14850, where queryCaveGeometry switches corridor (-6.22) to chamber (-7.70) with one nets list. The sweep's in-cave walk-in breaks (1.5-2.0 h step-ups at along -24..-120, picker -> {topH:0, idx:-1}, L7901) are consistent with this.

new_findings.summary: D1 has a third cause: the feather slope itself is steeper than STEP_UP where it overrides the approach ramp
new_findings.evidence: A probe giving each entrance's approach its own corridor depth instead of e.depth||5 (L4741) fixes 5 of the 8 failing entrance paths. Unifying tree depth as well still leaves 3/9. Example: n999983 r3,-4 e#0 along 224->206 goes -3.90 -> -5.25 because chamber fade jumps 0.593 -> 0.733 in one cell. The smoothstep over 0.3r+108 u (L4702) for an 8-11 h drop gives up to ~1.35 h per 12 u cell, and the chamber wins because bestFade > approachFade.

new_findings.summary: STEP_DOWN is relaxed only within 260 u of an entrance (L7853), but the approach ramp is 480 u long (APPROACH_LEN L4661)
new_findings.evidence: In the --networks all sweep, walk-in is unsupported at along +260 (n424242 r9,12 e#1: h -1.28 -> -2.45) and +278 (n999983 r9,-1 e#0: -2.11 -> -3.37). Under the rng2 probe world it also breaks at along +320 (n424242 r-3,6: -1.24 -> -2.56). The default worlds do not hit it.

new_findings.summary: The code comment at assembleWindow L6655-6660 ('Z always ends up above the ceiling because ... ceiling < surface - 0.5') is false for thousands of cells
new_findings.evidence: 4,555 caps across the 6 default windows only sit above their ceiling because of the L6693 clamp, which raised them above the natural surfaceH by up to +2.24 h (ct777 at (174,798)). The depth gate uses the chunk-clipped 21x21 MAX surface (L5595-5604), not the local surface. Dropping the clamp gives 2,966 caps at or below their ceiling.

new_findings.summary: spawnGoal can throw instead of placing a goal. It seeds its LCG with rs=(Date.now()^0xBEEF)|0 (4085). When that is negative, % keeps the sign, rng() stays in (-1,0], candidates[negative] is undefined and 'pick.x' throws a TypeError at 4104. _pt swallows the exception, and because enemies is already empty, updateEnemies returns early (11312) on every later frame, so spawnGoal is never retried. On a FIXED level the exit therefore never appears and the level cannot be completed. The sign flips every 2^31 ms (about 24.9 days), and it is negative on 2026-09-18.
new_findings.evidence: Scratch run on fixed level 1 via LAB.startLevel + LAB.frame. Clock 1700000000000 (int32=-807020850): all 6 enemies die, _ptErrors.gameUpdate=1, goal=null after 30 frames. Clock 2026-09-18T12:00Z (int32=-1268516658): same result. Clock +2^31 (int32=+1340462798): goal spawned at (1274,158). In the suite's Endless check, s424242 at Date.now()=1802147483648 gives 'spawnGoal threw TypeError inside spawnGoal'.

new_findings.summary: The Settings panel's Day/Night toggle hit area overlaps the Apply button. handleSettingsClick takes the first matching area, so a click on the upper 55% of Apply toggles Day/Night instead of applying, and the panel stays open. The panel height is min(260*S, 0.92*h) with h=240*S, so it is always height-clamped and the overlap happens at every resolution.

audit_contradictions: [D24] says Endless spawns a fixed-level goal when all enemies in the window die. That holds for only half of all clock values. When int32(Date.now()^0xBEEF) < 0 (the harness's default virtual clock 1.7e12, and real time on 2026-09-18), spawnGoal throws a TypeError at 4104 and no goal appears. Evidence: the suite's two-clock run on s424242 gives goalSpawned=true at Date.now()=1800000000000 and 'threw TypeError inside spawnGoal' at 1802147483648. The first draft of this scenario crashed on exactly that exception.

[D23] quotes 41 -> 74 enemies. The mechanism reproduces, but the numbers do not match the default seed. On 424242, an Apply with no edits takes the world census (window array plus cached-chunk lists) from 36 to 60 with no kills, or 33 to 57 after 3 border kills, with 22-24 duplicate pairs. The live window array goes 36 -> 32. The audit's seed or counting method is unknown, so this may only be a different measurement.
concerns: Scenario isolation: resetEndlessMode leaks spells, fortressAllies, completedFortresses and WINDOW_CHUNKS (the last only after an Apply). The restart scenario measures these leaks first. After that, freshWorld() restores them from page-load snapshots so later scenarios do not inherit them.

The market/shrine guarantee only fires when grid is null. For seeds after the first in a --seeds run, the restart scenario sets grid=null before world 1 to emulate a page load. The first seed really is the page's first world, and PAGE_GRID_WAS_NULL is checked.

The arena and spawner flag checks set arenaEnemy/fromSpawner directly on live enemies, because the 424242 spawn window has no spawner or altar. The underground check uses enemies that Cave Test's generator marks underground.
The shared ctx stub has no arcTo/roundRect, and drawSettingsOverlay throws without them. The harness wraps the game's ctx global in a local Proxy only for that call.

Game physics is not bit-identical across engines: in a multi-seed run, earlier walks took a different number of ticks on deno and jsc, which shifted the virtual clock. Details therefore never print tick counts or clock-dependent values, and the Endless-goal scenario sets the clock to absolute values (1.8e12 + k*2^31) through LAB.advance. After that fix, default and 4-seed sweep outputs match exactly on deno and jsc.

On seed 12345 (normal Endless), walls block a straight real-input walk in all four headings. The delta-growth scenario then falls back to a guided straight line (placeWorld steps at 90 u/s, one real tick per step) and says so in the detail.

The 'no information' criterion for delta records is a record whose every field is empty, false or all-zero. It follows the task's stated desire, but it would also fail an implementation that keeps zero records under some other memory bound. Growth is reported separately as METRICs.

Not covered: the spawnersDestroyed and shrineUsed deltas after eviction (the 424242 spawn window has no spawner and only an injected shrine), stats/toastLog/mapRevealAnim not being reset on an Endless restart (unclear whether they should be), and a Settings Apply that really changes the window size (e.g. to 'ultra').

FIX probes for killed-enemy revival, swap eviction, the arena/spawner flags and the guaranteed-feature eviction were not written. Each needs edits in two places, and probe_testcase takes a single anchor.

Enemies can shove the walker across a chunk line (seed 12345 far2: 450/600 frames in-chunk). The play checks therefore count only in-chunk frames and require at least 300 of them; a world where enemies pin the player could still fail that precondition.
Once the fixed-level floor crash is fixed (probe 01), each Level 4 sweep pass renders about 46k cells, which adds roughly 10 s to the default run (still under 60 s on deno).
The walk-speed check measures 1 s from rest, so it includes acceleration. The 5% tolerance held (ratio 1.012) under the real-dt fix probe.

In actual play only 27/118 cave enemies (22.9%) walk 20 u or less, because separation shoves from chamber-mates keep degenerate cave enemies walking back to their waypoints. The surface figure matches the audit exactly: 42/222 = 18.9%.
'The AI decides every 80 ms with a step of speed*0.08 per decision' holds for chase only (L11441). Patrol steps speed*0.38*0.08 per decision (L11299).
concerns: Patrol, chase and separation use a direct enemy pipeline (updateDayNight + updateEnemies + separateEnemies, i.e. gameUpdate L19404/L19406-19407) with the reference player set without updateChunks. A fix that moves enemy logic into another gameUpdate step would not be exercised by those checks. The roof, traversal-walk and re-centre checks use the full LAB.tick/walkTo.
Patrol keeps chase off by setting shopMarker on the reference point (the game's own market-safe rule, L11420). updateGuardTower is deliberately not run.
The traversal check relocates a real surface enemy and overrides its waypoints to [B, A]. The separation check relocates real enemies into clusters. Both are scaffolding built from game objects.
The waypoint-span threshold (28 u) is tied to the arrival radius constant at L11295. If a fix changes that radius, the threshold must change with it.
The Z check (PASS) cannot see z going stale after movement when the flag is lost, because chamber floors are flat. The flag check carries D19.

The roof check's placeWorld may re-centre the window, which triggers D19. A fix based on the underground flag alone would pass only once D19 is also fixed. This is deliberate, to stay faithful to play. The LOS FIX probe uses a z-difference heuristic instead.
The ring FIX probe is crude: it changes isInGridWall for every Z-less caller while the player is on the surface, which would also let cave enemies pass cave walls. It only demonstrates the cause.
The default run contains only 2 embedded enemies, both in the 424242 cave window. Detection power for F3 is low on the default seeds; --seeds widens it.

new_findings.summary: ceilSkipLowCeil is incremented for every non-ceiling layer of every in-view cell. caveCapture and the stats panel therefore report thousands of 'skipped low ceilings' in a window that has no ceilings at all.
new_findings.evidence: L13021. Seed 12345 at world (-1880,720), 0 type-2 layers in the whole 280x280 mesh: ceilPipeline skipLowCeil 6046, and 'visited' 22952 is the sum of per-layer and per-cell counters. The same on 4 of 4 seeds.

new_findings.summary: The control map colours each cell by l0TopZ, so cells whose l0 is a buried ceiling are painted as cave floor although their only walkable layers are at the surface.
new_findings.evidence: L21641, with the Z-sort at L6724. Seed 12345: 428 of 3,238 underground-painted cells, e.g. world (672,480) stack 2@-0.51 1@1.17 4@1.18 painted rgb(37,46,95). 1,203 cells over 4 seeds. The 'has ceiling, floor at surface' teal colour is never used (0 cells), because ceilings are negative. A FIX probe (lowest walkable layer) flips it to PASS.

new_findings.summary: For W and N wall faces, caveGaps and the wallFaceBase precompute sample the column/row one cell past the face vertex. A floor drop at a W/N face's far vertex is invisible to both; E and S faces are sampled correctly.
new_findings.evidence: L1549-1554 and L6856-6865, with a 1 u offset into the neighbour. On all 4 seeds, dropping the far-vertex floor 2 h below the base is not reported for W/N faces (seed 12345: W (140,123)/(140,124), N (130,122)/(131,122)) but is reported for E/S faces. Setting off = 0.0 flips it to PASS. On the unmodified world caveGaps finds 0 gaps over 50 faces (max gap -6.02 h), because cave walls are also pushed to the window's min floor - 0.5 (L6875-6893).

audit_contradictions: debugCaveAt with its hardcoded smoothedSurface 2.0 (L4802) agrees with the mesh on Cave Test seed 12345 at every core cell: 0 of 1,631 wrong, worst 0.010 h. Seeds 777 and 424242 also give 0 mismatches. The hardcode only shows where the stamper's real smoothed surface is below 2.0 (seed 1: 36 core cells, 0.47 h, e.g. mesh 1@-6.58 2@0.20 vs debugCaveAt -6.31/0.47). So the check fails only because seed 1 is in its default seeds. Separately, in feather cells debugCaveAt's caveFloorZ is the blend target, which differs from the stamped floor in 88.7% of cells; that is by design, since the tool also reports fade.

Clarification, not a contradiction: network entrances do carry no depth (L4486), but deepCaveEntrances, which caveCapture/caveDiag/the stats panel read, do carry depth and ceilH (L7160-7161). The seed 12345 capture shows entrances.0.depth=7.62 and ceilH=6.4, so the tools' entrance-table depth column is populated.
concerns: P1 builds its ground truth from the chart's documented sampling (60 points from -60 u to entrance+300 u, L21362-21370) and identifies the ceiling line by its colour #cc9955. A fix that recolours the line would read as 'no ceiling drawn'.

M1 inverts the control map's linear cell placement (pxPerUnit = width/1000, centred on the nearest entrance) and treats blue-dominant rgb() as the underground palette. The inversion is validated (0 off-grid rects of 7,225), but it depends on that layout.

G2's floor drop is an in-memory mutation of floorMesh (restored afterwards). It proves the W/N sampling geometry; it does not show that such drops occur naturally. On the unmodified world caveGaps never reports a gap, by construction.
X1 fails only because seed 1 is in the default seed list. `--seeds 12345` alone makes it PASS, and KNOWN_BUGS is keyed to the default run.
S2 treats the floor histogram as a partition because both displays show its buckets as a percentage of 'total visited'. The code comment calls blendRange 'layer-stitch successes'.

F1-F3 set the flag variables directly; the checkbox handlers are one-line assignments at L22240-22242, and the real 'change' listener is not fired. The A/B signature sees fills, ctx counters and logs but not fillText, so a flag that only changes HUD text (e.g. DEBUG_3D, L17512) would read as 'no change'.

The C1/C2/D2/P2 standing samples are one column per entrance (along -100). The default seed 12345 has one entrance, so each check has 2 samples, 1 on the cap and 1 on the cave floor. Preconditions require at least one of each.
LAB.startCaveTest does not reseed Math.random (startEndless does), so the harness calls LAB.seedRandom(seed) after it to stay deterministic.
window.caveTest (L1720) is async and uses awaited setTimeout waits, so a synchronous harness cannot drive it. It is untested.
env_requests: LAB.record should also capture stroke() (style and path), fillRect and fillText on the main canvas. fillText is currently a silent, uncounted no-op, so text-only debug effects are invisible to an A/B frame comparison.

A LAB.recordCanvas(id, fn) helper, i.e. a recording 2D context for secondary element canvases such as #caveProfileCanvas and #controlMapCanvas. Their contexts are no-op offscreen stubs today; this harness builds one locally.
Capture addEventListener on getElementById stubs (keyed by element id and event type), so a harness can fire the real checkbox 'change' handler instead of assigning the flag.
A microtask/async pump, e.g. a LAB.drain() the harness can await or a sync job queue, to drive async page functions such as window.caveTest.
LAB.startCaveTest(seed) should reseed Math.random, as startEndless does.
